name: Mibzar
overview: Mibzar was a male Edomite who held the position of chief within the tribe of Edom. His leadership role is specifically noted in Genesis 36:42, identifying him as a significant figure among the descendants of Esau. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Mibzar means 'bastion,' indicating a possible connotation of strength or defense. This proper name was not given by God but is recorded in Genesis 36:42. No other titles or names are associated with him in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Mibzar was a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. Beyond this, no further family relationships or genealogical details are provided in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Mibzar's significance lies in his role as a chief of Edom, highlighting the established leadership structure among Esau's descendants. His mention in Genesis 36:42 situates him within the broader narrative of the Edomite chiefs, reflecting the ongoing development of the nations descended from Esau. Though brief, his inclusion underscores the biblical emphasis on genealogies and tribal governance within God's providential plan.
